key_facts: The meeting is the seventh of the Special Committee on the COVID-19 Pandemic.
Mr. Paul Manly presented a petition calling for a ban on cosmetic testing using animals, following the EU model.
Hon. Pierre Poilievre tabled e-petition 2466 with 827 signatures, advocating for mandatory life jackets for children under 14 on small vessels.

Hon. Andrew Scheer questioned the government about ignoring 200,000 cases of suspected fraud in benefit applications; Prime Minister Justin Trudeau emphasized detecting and recovering fraudulent funds.
Trudeau reaffirmed the government’s one China policy but supports Taiwan's meaningful inclusion in international bodies like the WHO.

Yves-François Blanchet asked if health care is in provincial jurisdiction and requested clarification on increasing health transfers to Quebec and other provinces; Patty Hajdu affirmed health as provincial jurisdiction and mentioned ongoing discussions.
Jagmeet Singh criticized the government for not addressing long-term care home issues adequately; Trudeau reiterated support for provincial efforts.

Poilievre pressed on how many ERB cheques were sent to those flagged as fraudulent; Jean-Yves Duclos stated 7.7 million Canadians received at least one payment without confirming the number of fraudulent cases.
Poilievre also asked about prisoners receiving benefits; Duclos denied that while others noted reports suggesting otherwise.
Anita Anand stated the government is diversely sourcing and building domestic capacity for PPE.
Navdeep Bains confirmed changes to CEBA eligibility criteria but did not commit to further modifications for owner-operators or dividend-based businesses.
Marie-Claude Bibeau addressed concerns about farm families and processing capacity bottlenecks but pointed to existing programs.
John Barlow highlighted survey results showing many businesses failed to qualify for any government program and urged expansion of eligibility.
Pat Kelly questioned the government's funding of the Office of the Auditor General, citing insufficient resources; Jean-Yves Duclos claimed increased funding and staff.
Michael Chong raised a potential criminal breach of the Statistics Act due to early leak of labor force data; Navdeep Bains called it unacceptable and pledged cooperation with investigations.
Blanchet sought confirmation of permanent and unconditional health transfer increases to provinces; Hajdu referenced past investments but gave no new commitment.
Marilne Gill highlighted struggles of seasonal industries in Quebec and asked for tailored assistance; Navdeep Bains acknowledged challenges and ongoing efforts.
Jagmeet Singh pushed for commitments to exclude companies in tax havens from public aid; Bill Morneau defended current measures and international cooperation.
Greg McLean critiqued the CECRA program for favoring landlords with mortgages and questioned conflict of interest involving BlackRock; Morneau defended the program as mutually beneficial.
Pierre Poilievre repeatedly asked about Canada's national debt and balance sheet details; Morneau avoided providing concrete figures.
Maxime Blanchette-Joncas discussed the failure of the rent assistance program for seasonal businesses; Bill Morneau dismissed criticism as premature.
Scott Duvall raised concerns about seniors’ financial insecurity and delayed disability support; Deb Schulte outlined temporary payments but no long-term solution.
